page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The underlying hardware integrates 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, with instruction set support including AVX-512, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, contains no bundled local disk storage, and excludes discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results situate the instance in lower performance brackets relative to modern cloud hardware profiles. In stress-ng testing, it records a single-core CPU score of 1103.19 and a multi-core score of 2934.50, placing both within the bottom 25%. Geekbench evaluations show a single-core score of 987.0 and a multi-core score of 2173.0. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate throughput of 20.58 GB/sec for uncached large block reads (bottom 10%) and 18.68 GB/sec for large block writes. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at 19.02 GB/sec, while PassMark database operations yield 1094.48 points, reflecting throughput constraints under sustained compute and memory-intensive execution.

The ecs.c5.xlarge provides an economical profile for applications requiring dedicated vCPU allocation without high RAM overhead. Because local disk storage is absent, persistent data operations rely entirely on external block storage devices. This instance configuration is appropriate for light microservices, lightweight web servers, basic continuous integration build tasks, and low-footprint caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), it delivers a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio alongside 35 MB of L3 cache and a 2 Gbps baseline network speed. The instance omits local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the unit in the lower execution tiers, displaying bottom 25% CPU performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside bottom 10% memory bandwidth performance during uncached read operations. Offering cost-effective dedicated CPU allocation without excess RAM overhead, the ecs.c5.xlarge is designed for lightweight web serving, microservices hosting, basic CI/CD tasks, and low-footprint background processing.
